record.title: Rumichaca phased commercial protest blockade against tariff dispute, March 2026
record.scope: Rumichaca bridge and its road approaches; passenger and freight vehicles principally obstructed
record.direction: Vehicle movement between Colombia and Ecuador obstructed.
record.movement: Freight trucks, ordinary cars and passenger vehicles on the bridge route.
record.exceptions: Pedestrians and motorcycles could cross during at least the March 11 phase; pedestrian travel also documented March 18.
record.imposing_authority: Border commerce, customs-logistics and transport worker groups, initially on the Colombian side and later on both sides
record.enforcement: Workers used trucks, other vehicles and wooden platforms on bridge approaches; structures removed at reopening.
record.consequences: Reduced customs activity and interrupted freight and passenger transport; unverified loss totals excluded.
record.relationship: Promotes R4-AM-L005. Separate from AM046 March 7 election measure, R4-AM-005 Ecuador selected-crossing regime, and R4-AM-002 February 2025 indigenous blockade. Initial brief actions and subsequent phases kept together as one protest family.
record.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
record.official_rationale: Protesters demanded removal of reciprocal tariffs and other restrictions they said damaged cross-border work and commerce.
record.context: This non-state protest followed the governments’ tariff dispute; it is distinct from the preceding Colombian election closure and Ecuador’s selected-crossing policy.
record.uncertainty: The often-repeated nineteen days is an inclusive protest-period description, not verified uninterrupted closure. Onset-day short actions and later restarts are explicit; Colombian and Ecuadorian sides joined at different times. Full daily exceptions are unknown.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Protest phases March 9–27; actual reopening March 27. Pauses, changing vehicle access and pedestrian/motorcycle exceptions rule out a continuous nineteen-day interval.
